--
-- A move with 0 base power leaves CalculateDamage with a == 0, and
-- PlayerCalcMoveDamage jumps straight to PlayerCheckIfFlyOrChargeEffect
-- (engine/battle/core.asm:3145; enemy twin :5507).  That routine opens
-- `ld c, 30 / call DelayFrames` (:3185-3186 / :5587-5588) and plays NO
-- animation -- GetPlayerAnimationType is never reached for these moves.
-- The animation a status move does show comes later, from its effect
-- handler's PlayCurrentMoveAnimation2 (engine/battle/effects.asm:1448),
-- which JumpMoveEffect reaches only AFTER those 30 frames.

-- GROWL!" and the first frame of the animation, and pays it whether the
-- effect goes on to land, fail or miss.  The port paid it only on a
-- damaging move's miss (EffectRegistry's missBeat), so every status move
-- in the game ran 30 frames short and fired its animation half a second

-- call: core.asm:3124-3127 sends them to JumpMoveEffect BEFORE
-- PlayerCalcMoveDamage, so they never reach the hold at all.  The list is
-- data/battle/residual_effects_1.asm, verbatim and in its own order.

  SWITCH_AND_TELEPORT_EFFECT = true, MIST_EFFECT = true,
  FOCUS_ENERGY_EFFECT = true, CONFUSION_EFFECT = true, HEAL_EFFECT = true,
  TRANSFORM_EFFECT = true, LIGHT_SCREEN_EFFECT = true, REFLECT_EFFECT = true,
  POISON_EFFECT = true, PARALYZE_EFFECT = true, SUBSTITUTE_EFFECT = true,
  MIMIC_EFFECT = true, LEECH_SEED_EFFECT = true, SPLASH_EFFECT = true,
}

--- Pay PlayerCheckIfFlyOrChargeEffect's hold for a 0 BP move, in the place
-- the hardware pays it: after the "used MOVE!" line and BEFORE the move's
-- animation row, so cancelling the animation afterwards (a failed or
-- missed effect) leaves the hold standing, exactly as the asm does.
function BattleState:statusMoveBeat(move)
  if move and RESIDUAL_EFFECTS_1[move.effect] then return end
  local at
  for i, item in ipairs(self.queue) do
    if item == self.moveAnimRow then at = i break end
  end
  self.nextInsert = (self.nextInsert or 0) + 1
  table.insert(self.queue, at or self.nextInsert,
               { wait = Timing.MOVE_STATUS_OR_MISS })
end

-- ------- storage that is FULL, and the Pokemon that used to be destroyed
--
-- ItemUseBall asks whether there is anywhere to put a catch BEFORE the ball
-- leaves the player's hand (item_effects.asm: wPartyCount == PARTY_LENGTH and
-- wNumInBox == MONS_PER_BOX -> BoxFullCannotThrowBallText -> ItemUseFailed,
-- so the ball is not spent, the turn is not taken, and the bag comes back).
-- This port never asked: it threw, caught, marked the dex, said "But every
-- BOX is full!" and dropped the Pokemon on the floor -- the ONE state the
-- cartridge is careful never to reach.  Three seams put it back:
--
--   catchStorageHasRoom()   the pre-throw question, asked by the bag and by
--                           the Safari menu.  Party, then every box, then
--                           whatever `catch.storage_room` claims it can hold.
--   overflowCaughtMon()     the commit: `catch.storage_overflow` takes the
--                           Pokemon and returns the line that names where it
--                           went.  A mod that answers it OWNS the Pokemon
--                           from that moment and must have persisted it.
--   refuseCaughtMon()       the backstop.  Nothing took it, so nothing is
--                           claimed either: the dex bits go back exactly as
--                           they were, the ball is refunded, and the battle
--                           ends as "run".  With the pre-throw gate in place
--                           this is reachable only when a storage mod said it
--                           had room and then did not take the Pokemon.
--
-- Any Pokemon reaching `refuseCaughtMon` is one the game could not keep, and
-- it is deliberately NOT recorded as caught -- an un-owned dex entry is a
-- recoverable annoyance, a Pokemon that the save says you own and no box
-- holds is not.

--- Is there anywhere at all for a caught Pokemon to go, right now?
function BattleState:catchStorageHasRoom()
  local save = self.game and self.game.save
  if not save then return true end
  if #(save.party or {}) < Party.MAX then return true end
  -- a mod that claims party-full catches decides for itself; the gate must
  -- not refuse a throw on behalf of storage it has taken over
  if Runtime.wantsHook("catch.party_full") then return true end
  local Boxes = require("src.pokemon.Boxes")
  local boxes = Boxes.ensure(save)
  for i = 1, Boxes.COUNT do
    if #(boxes[i] or {}) < Boxes.CAPACITY then return true end
  end
  if Runtime.wantsHook("catch.storage_room") then
    local room = Runtime.call("catch.storage_room", function() return false end,
      { battle = self, game = self.game,
        mon = self.enemy and self.enemy.mon,
        name = self.enemy and self.enemy.name })
    if room then return true end
  end
  return false
end

--- Hand the Pokemon to whatever storage claims it.  Returns the message that
--- names where it went, or nil if nothing took it.
function BattleState:overflowCaughtMon(mon)
  if not Runtime.wantsHook("catch.storage_overflow") then return nil end
  local taken = Runtime.call("catch.storage_overflow", function() return nil end,
    { battle = self, game = self.game, mon = mon,
      species = mon and mon.species,
      name = self.enemy and self.enemy.name })
  if type(taken) == "string" and taken ~= "" then return taken end
  if taken then
    return Strings("%s was\ntransferred to\nextended storage!", self.enemy.name)
  end
  return nil
end

-- ------- one palette for the whole animation, on a Game Boy Color
--
-- The zone lookup below is a SUPER GAME BOY.  That machine colours the
-- composited DMG picture and cannot tell an OBJ pixel from a BG one, so a
-- beam really does change colour crossing an ATTR_BLK boundary
-- (data/sgb/sgb_packets.asm:61) and `zoneColorsAt` is right for SGB mode.
--
-- A Game Boy Color does not work that way, and Yellow ships real CGB code.
-- SetAnimationPalette's `.notSGB` arm (pokeyellow engine/battle/animations.asm
-- :589-597) writes rOBP0 = $e4, rOBP1 = $6c and calls UpdateCGBPal_OBP0/1;
-- InitCGBPalettes (engine/gfx/palettes.asm:736) builds OBJ palettes 0-3 from
-- the four base palettes through OBP0.  So on hardware a sprite's colour does
-- NOT change as it crosses an ATTR_BLK boundary: it wears whichever CGB OBJ
-- palette its OAM attribute byte names, for as long as it is on screen.
--
-- Which one that is depends on the cartridge, and the two Gen 1 engines
-- differ -- see animObjPalIndex below.  pokered's DrawFrameBlock copies the
-- frame block's flags byte verbatim (only OAM_PAL1, a DMG bit the CGB
-- ignores, is ever set there), so red and blue leave the CGB palette bits at
-- 0 and every animation sprite reads base palette 0.  pokeyellow keeps an
-- attribute byte in wdef4 and picks base palette 2 or 3 by screen half.
--
-- Which palette: the cartridge's own colours for the Pokemon the animation
-- belongs to, so a Thundershock is the attacker's yellow end to end rather
-- than yellow over its box and the player's HP-bar green everywhere else
-- (user report 2026-08-29: "part of the bolts ... yellow but part is broken
-- green").  Hardware would use base palette 0 -- the player's HP bar -- for
-- everything; per-attacker is the user's own call, taken because it keeps
-- the variation between cartridges that a single global palette throws away.
-- `battle.anim_palette` lets a mod refine that to the exact source cartridge.
function BattleState:animUsesObjPalette()
  local PaletteFX = require("src.render.PaletteFX")
  return PaletteFX.usesGbcPack() or PaletteFX.usesYellowCgb()
end

-- ------- which CGB OBJ palette an animation sprite wears, from its OAM X
--
-- pokered has none of this: its DrawFrameBlock copies the frame block's
-- flags byte into OAM verbatim (pokered engine/battle/animations.asm:3-100),
-- so the CGB palette bits stay 0 and every animation sprite reads base
-- palette 0.
--
-- pokeyellow is a real Game Boy Color game and DOES set them.  Its
-- DrawFrameBlock keeps the attribute byte in wdef4: `ld a, $2 /
-- ld [wdef4], a` at the top of the per-tile loop, then, immediately after
-- the X byte is stored, `cp 88 / jr c, .. / ld a, [wdef4] / inc a /
-- ld [wdef4], a`, and finally `ld a, [wdef4] / or b / ld [de], a` into the
-- OAM flags -- pokeyellow engine/battle/animations.asm:18-19, :51-56,
-- :63-67, with the same three steps repeated in the HVFLIP arm (:86-90,
-- :108-110) and the HFLIP arm (:128-132, :148-150).  So a sprite whose OAM
-- X is below 88 wears CGB OBJ palette 2, and one at or above it wears 3.
--
-- InitCGBPalettes (engine/gfx/palettes.asm:736-776) builds OBJ palette N
-- from BASE palette N through rOBP0, and SetPal_Battle (:28-65) fills the
-- four base slots with [0] the player's HP bar, [1] the enemy's HP bar,
-- [2] the PLAYER's mon palette and [3] the ENEMY's mon palette -- the same
-- order sgbBattlePals answers in.  A battle animation on Yellow therefore
-- wears the player's mon colours on the left half of the screen and the
-- enemy's on the right, never base palette 0.
--
-- This is INVISIBLE for the whole of any subanimation, which is where every
-- attack lives: wAnimPalette is $f0 there, $f0 reads only base colour 0 and
-- base colour 3, and every CGBBasePalettes row opens on 31,31,31 and closes
-- on 03,03,03 (data/sgb/sgb_palettes.asm:46-87).  It is what the Poke Ball
-- LEFT ON THE GROUND after a capture shows, once rOBP0 has been popped back
-- to $e4 -- see animSpriteColors' `resting` arm.
BattleState.ANIM_OBJ_PAL_SPLIT = 88

function BattleState:animObjPalIndex(x)
  if not require("src.core.GameVersion").isYellow() then return 0 end
  if type(x) ~= "number" then return 2 end
  return x >= BattleState.ANIM_OBJ_PAL_SPLIT and 3 or 2
end

-- The palette, resolved once per frame and screen half -- animSpriteColors
-- runs per sprite per attribute cell, and neither sgbBattlePals nor a hook
-- chain belongs in that loop.
function BattleState:animPalette(x)
  local idx = self:animObjPalIndex(x)
  if self._animPalFrame == self.frame and self._animPalIdx == idx
     and self._animPal ~= nil then
    return self._animPal or nil, self._animPalHooked
  end
  local isPlayer = self.animAttackerIsPlayer and true or false
  local pals = self:sgbBattlePals()
  -- CGB OBJ palette idx == base palette idx; see animObjPalIndex above
  local fallback = pals and pals[idx]
  local P, hooked = fallback, false
  if Runtime.wantsHook("battle.anim_palette") then
    -- The vanilla link returns nil, not fallback.  A wrapper that merely
    -- calls next_() has declined the enhancement and must not make the valid
    -- fallback table look like a custom answer (which would lift $f0 to $e4).
    -- `ctx.default` still exposes the fallback to a mod that wants to derive
    -- an explicit palette from it.
    local ok, answer = pcall(Runtime.call, "battle.anim_palette",
      function() return nil end, self,
      { attacker = isPlayer and self.player or self.enemy,
        attackerIsPlayer = isPlayer, move = self.animName,
        -- which ball this animation belongs to, or nil for a move.  The
        -- running animation's own item first; `lastBall` behind it because the
        -- ball PARKED ON THE GROUND after a capture outlives the animation
        -- that drew it (see the `resting` arm below) and by then animBall has
        -- moved on with the chain.  A mod that colours a ball must still gate
        -- on `move` naming a ball animation -- `lastBall` stays set for the
        -- rest of the battle.
        ball = self.animBall or self.lastBall,
        default = fallback })
    -- four RGB triples or nothing: a mod that answers something else gets
    -- the engine's own palette rather than a crash mid-draw
    if ok and type(answer) == "table" and #answer == 4 then
      local good = true
      for i = 1, 4 do
        local c = answer[i]
        if type(c) ~= "table" or type(c[1]) ~= "number"
           or type(c[2]) ~= "number" or type(c[3]) ~= "number" then
          good = false break
        end
      end
      if good then P, hooked = answer, true end
    end
  end
  self._animPal, self._animPalFrame = P or false, self.frame
  self._animPalIdx = idx
  self._animPalHooked = hooked
  return P, hooked
end

function BattleState:animSpriteColors(s, px, py, resting)
  -- ------- $f0 or $e4: SetAnimationPalette's OWN branch, not a constant
  --
  -- AnimPlayer stamps every animation sprite `f0` (or `f0x` mid-strobe)
  -- because that is what wAnimPalette is on the machine this port usually
  -- models.  It is not what it is on all of them.  SetAnimationPalette
  -- (pokeyellow engine/battle/animations.asm:565-571, pokered :551-557) is:
  --
  --     ld a, [wOnSGB]
  --     and a
  --     ld a, $e4
  --     jr z, .notSGB        ; wOnSGB = 0 -> the IDENTITY ramp
  --     ld a, $f0            ; wOnSGB = 1 -> white and black
  --     ld [wAnimPalette], a
  --
  -- and `onSgb()` above is already that flag, resolved for the display mode:
  -- pokeyellow's LoadSGB (engine/gfx/palettes.asm:543-556) sets it on a Game
  -- Boy Color as well as a Super Game Boy -- `jr c, .onSGB / ldh a, [hOnCGB] /
  -- and a / jr z, .onDMG / ld a, $1` -- while POKERED's (:392-402) does not:
  --
  --     call CheckSGB
  --     ret nc               ; not an SGB -> RETURN, wOnSGB still 0
  --     ld a, 1
  --     ld [wOnSGB], a
  --
  -- The `ret nc` fires first, so a Game Boy Color running RED or BLUE through
  -- its boot ROM -- which is what OG RED / OG BLUE / OG GREEN model, and what
  -- usesSpriteObp is true for -- leaves the flag at 0 and takes $e4.  So does
  -- a plain Game Boy (OG / OG INV / CLASSIC): CheckSGB fails and there is no
  -- hOnCGB to rescue it.
  --
  -- $f0 sends sprite colour 1 to base colour 0 and colours 2 and 3 to base
  -- colour 3.  Every boot-pair OBJ ramp is white at index 0 and black at index
  -- 3 (PaletteFX.GBC_OBJ, GBC_OBJ_BLUE, SPRITE_VARIETY OgCart.GREEN_OBJ), so
  -- forcing $f0 in those modes threw away the whole ramp and drew a Poke Ball
  -- as a white circle with a black band -- in a mode whose entire point is
  -- that the Game Boy Color boot ROM colourises the cartridge.  With the
  -- hardware branch restored, OG RED draws it in the boot ROM's green

-- Type-tagged, deterministic and bounded: full headers/options are represented,
-- including unrecognised fields, rather than trusting a hand-picked blob hash.
local function canonical(value)
  local out, seen, bytes = {}, {}, 0
  local function append(s)
    bytes = bytes + #s
    assert(bytes <= MAX_IDENTITY, "Prepared identity exceeds bound")
    out[#out + 1] = s
  end
  local function encode(v, depth)
    assert(depth < 32, "Prepared identity nesting exceeds bound")
    local kind = type(v)
    if kind == "nil" then append("z")
    elseif kind == "boolean" then append(v and "t" or "f")
    elseif kind == "number" then
      assert(v == v and v ~= math.huge and v ~= -math.huge, "Nonfinite identity")
      append("n" .. ("%.17g"):format(v) .. ";")
    elseif kind == "string" then append("s" .. #v .. ":" .. v)
    elseif kind == "table" then
      assert(not seen[v] and getmetatable(v) == nil, "Cyclic/metatable identity")
      seen[v] = true
      local keys = {}
      for k in pairs(v) do
        assert(type(k) == "string" or type(k) == "number", "Unsupported identity key")
        keys[#keys + 1] = k
        assert(#keys <= 8192, "Prepared identity table exceeds bound")
      end
      table.sort(keys, function(a, b)
        if type(a) ~= type(b) then return type(a) < type(b) end
        return a < b
      end)
      append("{")
      for _, k in ipairs(keys) do encode(k, depth + 1); encode(v[k], depth + 1) end
      append("}")
      seen[v] = nil
    else error("Unsupported identity value " .. kind) end
  end
  encode(value, 0)
  return table.concat(out)
end

local function readBounded(path, maximum)
  local info = fs.getInfo(path)
  assert(info and info.type == "file" and info.size > 0 and info.size <= maximum,
    "Absent or oversized prepared file")
  local bytes = assert(fs.read(path))
  assert(#bytes == info.size, "Prepared file changed while reading")
  return bytes
end

local function u16(n) return string.char(n % 256, math.floor(n / 256) % 256) end

function M.metadata(key, pcm)

local function parseMetadata(bytes, key)
  -- This is a deliberately strict, flat JSON schema. No code, paths, duplicate
  -- fields, trailing data, nested structures or permissive JSON coercions.
  local k, pcm, frames, size = bytes:match(
    '^%{"version":1,"key":"([0-9a-f]+)","pcm":"([0-9a-f]+)","frames":(%d+),"bytes":(%d+)%}\n$')
  frames, size = tonumber(frames), tonumber(size)
  assert(k == key and isHash(k) and isHash(pcm) and frames and size
    and frames >= 441 and frames <= M.MAX_FRAMES and size == frames * 4,
    "Invalid prepared metadata")

end

local function validateWav(wav, size)
  assert(#wav == size + 44 and wav:sub(1, 4) == "RIFF"
    and long(wav, 5) == size + 36 and wav:sub(9, 16) == "WAVEfmt "
    and long(wav, 17) == 16 and word(wav, 21) == 1 and word(wav, 23) == 2
    and long(wav, 25) == 44100 and long(wav, 29) == 176400
    and word(wav, 33) == 4 and word(wav, 35) == 16
    and wav:sub(37, 40) == "data" and long(wav, 41) == size,

local function checkedSoundData(wav, pcmHash, frames, size)

    enabled = jit and jit.status() or false, love = { love.getVersion() } }

  local strings, stringCount = {}, 0
  local function bankHash(bytes)
    assert(type(bytes) == "string" and #bytes <= 1024 * 1024, "Invalid bank input")
    if not strings[bytes] then
      stringCount = stringCount + 1
      assert(stringCount <= 256, "Prepared bank memo bound exceeded")
      strings[bytes] = digest(bytes)
    end
    return strings[bytes]
  end
  -- Immutable string contents may repeat across every decoder closure walk.
  -- Bound retained keys; when full, hash normally. Mutable graph traversal,
  -- source provenance and all emitted identity bytes remain unchanged.
  local captureStrings, captureCount, captureBytes = {}, 0, 0
  local function captureHash(bytes)
    local cached = captureStrings[bytes]
    if cached then return cached end
    local value = digest(bytes)
    if captureCount < 2048 and captureBytes + #bytes <= 4 * 1024 * 1024 then
      captureStrings[bytes] = value
      captureCount, captureBytes = captureCount + 1, captureBytes + #bytes
    end

  end

    if not code[fn] then
      local info = assert(getinfo(fn, "S"))
      assert(info.what == "Lua" and sourceAllowed(info.source), "Unknown live synthesis wrapper")
      -- Raw LuaJIT dumps randomize template hash order across processes.
      -- The bundled VM predates dump('d'); retain complete code identity by
      -- sorting only template hash pairs in a bounded stripped-dump parser.

    local methods, captures, visited, count = {}, {}, {}, 0
    -- Include functions captured by decoder wrappers (not just their source
    -- file), so swapping a helper on Gen2Sfx's module table changes identity.
    local function visit(value, path, depth)
      assert(depth < 16, "Synthesis closure nesting exceeds bound")
      local kind = type(value)
      if value == bitLibrary then captures[path] = "LuaJIT bit library"; return end
      if kind ~= "table" and kind ~= "function" then
        if kind == "string" then captures[path] = { stringHash = captureHash(value) }
        elseif kind == "number" or kind == "boolean" then captures[path] = value
        elseif kind ~= "nil" then error("Unknown live synthesis capture") end

      end
      if visited[value] then captures[path] = { reference = visited[value] }; return end
      visited[value] = path
      count = count + 1; assert(count <= 512, "Synthesis closure bound exceeded")

-- Loading-only PCM interning. Source definitions/provenance are NOT merged.
-- Hashes select a bucket; exact bytes AND format decide buffer equivalence.
-- Every key owns a separate Source playback handle, sharing immutable PCM.
local M = {}

function M.new(opts)
  assert(type(opts) == "table" and type(opts.hash) == "function"
    and type(opts.newSource) == "function", "Prepared source dependencies unavailable")
  local pool = { bytes = 0, buffers = 0, aliases = 0, buckets = {} }
  local maximum = opts.maxBytes or 96 * 1024 * 1024
  function pool:source(sd)
    local frames, rate = sd:getSampleCount(), sd:getSampleRate()
    local depth, channels = sd:getBitDepth(), sd:getChannelCount()
    assert(frames >= 1 and frames <= 220500 and frames % 1 == 0
      and rate > 0 and rate % 1 == 0 and depth == 16 and channels == 2,
      "Unexpected prepared PCM format")
    local bytes = sd:getString()
    assert(type(bytes) == "string" and #bytes == frames * channels * (depth / 8),
      "Prepared PCM byte count mismatch")
    local format = table.concat({ frames, rate, depth, channels }, ":")
    local digest = opts.hash(bytes)
    assert(type(digest) == "string", "Prepared PCM hash unavailable")
    local key = format .. ":" .. digest
    local bucket = self.buckets[key]
    for _, entry in ipairs(bucket or {}) do
      if entry.bytes == bytes then
        local clone = assert(entry.source:clone(), "Prepared Source clone unavailable")
        self.aliases = self.aliases + 1
        return clone, entry.token
      end
    end
    assert(self.bytes + #bytes <= maximum, "Prepared PCM pool memory bound exceeded")
    local source = assert(opts.newSource(sd, "static"), "Prepared Source unavailable")
    local token = {} -- remains valid after this temporary byte index is released
    local entry = { bytes = bytes, source = source, token = token }
    bucket = bucket or {}; self.buckets[key] = bucket
    bucket[#bucket + 1] = entry
    self.bytes, self.buffers = self.bytes + #bytes, self.buffers + 1
    return source, token
  end
  return pool
end

return M

local ACCEL_OFF, GYRO_OFF = 24, 30
local O_RDONLY, O_NONBLOCK = 0, 2048 -- Linux; O_NONBLOCK is 0o4000
local MAX_DRAIN = 64 -- headroom against a stalled frame; loop exits on EAGAIN
local RESCAN_PERIOD = 2.0 -- seconds between sysfs rescans / silent-node drops

-- chip's configured full-scale range is, so the constant below is measured
-- rather than taken from a datasheet.
--
-- ACCEL_COUNTS_PER_G was measured HERE, through this exact patch, on a
-- stationary Deck under a real Steam launch (review/w14-gyro-2026-08-29/

-- 31.45..31.58 m/s^2 (spread 0.4%, i.e. real sensor noise, not a frozen
-- value) against the OLD guess of 6062 counts/g -- which backs out a real
-- raw magnitude of ~19477 counts at rest, so that is the constant now.
-- 19477 is close to, but not exactly, the naive 16384-counts/g datasheet
-- assumption; whether that gap is this specific unit, firmware, or
-- temperature is unknown and does not matter for "physically sane," which
-- is the only bar this needs to clear (Motion.lua only ever consumes the
-- NORMALISED direction, never this absolute number). Imu.lua's own
-- comment about "~0.37 of 16384" describes a DIFFERENT measurement (that
-- mod's direct hidraw reader, before mod chunks were sandboxed away from
-- ffi) and is not reused here on purpose -- this constant is this patch's
-- own, on this path, dated to this session.

-- own regression) is kept as-is; the live run above measured only a
-- near-stationary Deck, which cannot calibrate a rotation rate.
local ACCEL_COUNTS_PER_G = 19477
local GYRO_COUNTS_PER_RADSEC = 2865
local GRAVITY = 9.80665

local hidrawCdefOk = nil
local hidrawLib = nil
local function hidrawFfi()
  local okFfi, ffi = pcall(require, "ffi")
  if not okFfi then return nil end
  if hidrawCdefOk == nil then

-- pace rescans without ever blocking a frame.
local hid = {

  rescanClock = 0, silentClock = 0, lastT = nil,
  accel = { 0, 0, 0 }, gyro = { 0, 0, 0 },

local function hidrawInt16(buf, off)
  local v = buf[off] + buf[off + 1] * 256

end

local function hidrawHeaderOk(buf)
  return buf[0] == 0x01 and buf[1] == 0x00 and buf[2] == 0x09 and buf[3] == 0x40
end

-- directories and cannot see /sys or /dev. Probing a fixed node range keeps
-- this free of io.popen -- an engine sensor read has no business spawning a
-- process every couple of seconds.
local function hidrawScan(lib)
  for i = 0, 15 do
    local f = io.open(("/sys/class/hidraw/hidraw%d/device/uevent"):format(i), "r")
    if f then
      local text = f:read("*a") or ""
      f:close()
      -- HID_ID=0003:000028DE:00001205 -- Valve, Steam Controller/Deck
      if text:find("28DE", 1, true) and text:find("1205", 1, true) then
        local path = ("/dev/hidraw%d"):format(i)
        local okOpen, fd = pcall(lib.open, path, O_RDONLY + O_NONBLOCK)
        if okOpen and fd and fd >= 0 then
          hid.candidates[#hid.candidates + 1] = { path = path, fd = fd }
        end
      end
    end
  end
  return #hid.candidates > 0

-- Drain one candidate; returns whether it produced a report we recognise.
-- Always copies whatever the IMU block currently says (including all
-- zeroes) into hid.accel/hid.gyro -- an honest zero IS the reading while
-- Steam Input is not asking for gyro, not a failure to hide.
local function hidrawDrain(lib, c)
  local sawReport = false
  for _ = 1, MAX_DRAIN do
    local okRead, n = pcall(lib.read, c.fd, hid.buf, 128)
    n = okRead and tonumber(n) or -1
    if n ~= REPORT then break end -- EAGAIN (-1) or a short/foreign report
    if hidrawHeaderOk(hid.buf) then
      sawReport = true
      local ax = hidrawInt16(hid.buf, ACCEL_OFF)
      local ay = hidrawInt16(hid.buf, ACCEL_OFF + 2)
      local az = hidrawInt16(hid.buf, ACCEL_OFF + 4)
      local gx = hidrawInt16(hid.buf, GYRO_OFF)
      local gy = hidrawInt16(hid.buf, GYRO_OFF + 2)
      local gz = hidrawInt16(hid.buf, GYRO_OFF + 4)
      hid.accel[1], hid.accel[2], hid.accel[3] =
        ax / ACCEL_COUNTS_PER_G * GRAVITY, ay / ACCEL_COUNTS_PER_G * GRAVITY,
        az / ACCEL_COUNTS_PER_G * GRAVITY
      hid.gyro[1], hid.gyro[2], hid.gyro[3] =
        gx / GYRO_COUNTS_PER_RADSEC, gy / GYRO_COUNTS_PER_RADSEC, gz / GYRO_COUNTS_PER_RADSEC
    end
  end
  return sawReport
end

-- Per-call pump: scans (throttled), drains whatever candidate(s) are open,
-- latches onto the first that speaks, and drops a node that has gone
-- silent so a future call rescans rather than reading a dead fd forever.
-- No sleep/wait anywhere in here, so nothing this can do stalls a frame.
local function hidrawUpdate()
  if not isLinux() then return false end
  local lib, ffi = hidrawFfi()
  if not lib then return false end
  if not hid.buf then hid.buf = ffi.new("uint8_t[?]", 128) end

  local now = (love and love.timer and love.timer.getTime and love.timer.getTime()) or 0
  local dt = hid.lastT and math.max(0, now - hid.lastT) or 0
  hid.lastT = now

  if not hid.chosen and #hid.candidates == 0 then
    hid.rescanClock = hid.rescanClock + dt
    if not hid.scanned or hid.rescanClock >= RESCAN_PERIOD then
      hid.scanned, hid.rescanClock = true, 0
      hidrawScan(lib)
    end
    if #hid.candidates == 0 then return false end
  end

  if hid.chosen then
    -- "no NEW report drained THIS call" is not the same fact as "the
    -- device has gone silent": DECK_TILT's own Imu.lua reads
    -- accelerometer immediately followed by gyroscope every single frame
    -- (pollEngine), and the controller streams reports at 250Hz against a
    -- ~60fps poll rate -- so the first of those two calls typically drains
    -- every report that has arrived since the last frame, and the second
    -- call that same tick legitimately sees nothing new (EAGAIN
    -- immediately). That is normal, not silence, and hid.accel/hid.gyro
    -- already hold the last decoded report either way -- returning them is
    -- the honest answer. Only a SUSTAINED silence (no fresh report for a
    -- full RESCAN_PERIOD of wall-clock time, which same-tick calls barely
    -- advance at all) means the node itself is actually gone.
    if hidrawDrain(lib, hid.chosen) then hid.silentClock = 0
    else hid.silentClock = hid.silentClock + dt end
    if hid.silentClock >= RESCAN_PERIOD then
      -- gone quiet: unplugged, or re-enumerated on a fresh node. Drop
      -- everything and let the next call scan again.
      pcall(lib.close, hid.chosen.fd)
      hid.candidates, hid.chosen, hid.silentClock = {}, nil, 0
      hid.rescanClock = RESCAN_PERIOD -- rescan on the very next call
      return false
    end
    return true
  end

  -- Race the candidates; the first to produce a recognised report wins and
  -- the rest are closed, same as Imu.lua's own latch().
  for _, c in ipairs(hid.candidates) do
    if hidrawDrain(lib, c) then
      for _, other in ipairs(hid.candidates) do
        if other ~= c then pcall(lib.close, other.fd) end
      end
      hid.candidates, hid.chosen = { c }, c
      return true
    end
  end
  return false
end
